transition.note: Mari Cordes resigned the seat in 2025 (the House directory records June 19, 2025). Governor Phil Scott appointed Karen Lueders to fill the vacancy on October 17, 2025.

sources.note: Office of Governor Phil Scott, press release (October 17, 2025), 'Governor Phil Scott Appoints Karen Lueders to the House of Representatives': the Governor appointed Karen Lueders of Lincoln to fill the vacant Addison-4 seat, replacing Mari Cordes, who resigned earlier in 2025.
Vermont General Assembly, All Representatives directory (2025-2026 session): marks Mari Cordes 'Resigned June 19, 2025' and lists Karen Lueders as an Addison-4 representative.

transition.note: Robert Hooper resigned the seat in 2026 (the House directory records March 16, 2026). Governor Phil Scott appointed Kevin Scully to fill the vacancy; the Governor's office lists the appointment among its second-quarter 2026 appointments (no dedicated appointment release was issued).

sources.note: Office of Governor Phil Scott, press release (July 22, 2026), 'Governor Phil Scott Announces 144 Appointments to State Boards and Commissions': under appointments made in the second quarter of 2026, lists 'Chittenden-18 District, House of Representatives -- Kevin Scully, Burlington'. No dedicated appointment release for this seat appears on governor.vermont.gov.
Vermont General Assembly, All Representatives directory (2025-2026 session): marks Robert Hooper 'Resigned March 16, 2026' and lists Kevin Scully as a Chittenden-18 representative.

transition.note: Chris Taylor resigned the seat in 2026 (the House directory records March 27, 2026). Governor Phil Scott appointed Kumulia Long to fill the vacancy, effective immediately on April 1, 2026.

sources.note: Office of Governor Phil Scott, press release (April 1, 2026), 'Governor Phil Scott Appoints Kumulia Long to House of Representatives': the Governor appointed Kumulia Long of Milton to fill the vacant Chittenden-Franklin seat, effective immediately.
Vermont General Assembly, All Representatives directory (2025-2026 session): marks Chris Taylor 'Resigned March 27, 2026' and lists Kumulia Long as a Chittenden-Franklin representative.

transition.note: Casey Toof resigned the seat in January 2026 (the House directory records January 16, 2026). Governor Phil Scott appointed John (Jack) Brigham to fill the vacancy, effective immediately on February 20, 2026.

sources.note: Office of Governor Phil Scott, press release (February 20, 2026), 'Governor Phil Scott Appoints Jack Brigham to House of Representatives': the Governor appointed John (Jack) Brigham of St. Albans Town to fill the vacant Franklin-8 seat, replacing Casey Toof, who resigned in January; the appointment is effective immediately.
Vermont General Assembly, All Representatives directory (2025-2026 session): marks Casey Toof 'Resigned Jan. 16, 2026' and lists Jack Brigham as the Franklin-8 representative.

transition.note: Jim Harrison resigned the seat effective January 6, 2026. Governor Phil Scott appointed Valorie Taylor (announced as Val Taylor) to fill the vacancy on January 2, 2026.

sources.note: Office of Governor Phil Scott, press release (January 2, 2026), 'Governor Phil Scott Announces Legislative Appointments': the Governor appointed Val Taylor to represent the Rutland-11 district in the House; Taylor replaces Representative Jim Harrison, who would be resigning effective January 6, 2026.
Vermont General Assembly, All Representatives directory (2025-2026 session): marks Jim Harrison 'Resigned Jan. 6, 2026' and lists Valorie Taylor as the Rutland-11 representative.

transition.note: Chris Brown resigned the seat in December 2024 (the House directory records December 13, 2024), before the 2025-2026 session convened. Governor Phil Scott appointed Zachary Harvey to fill the vacancy, effective January 8, 2025.

sources.note: Office of Governor Phil Scott, press release (January 7, 2025), 'Governor Phil Scott Appoints Zachary Harvey to the House of Representatives': the Governor appointed Zachary Harvey of Castleton to fill the vacant Rutland-3 seat, replacing Chris Brown, who resigned the month before; the appointment is effective January 8, 2025.
Vermont General Assembly, All Representatives directory (2025-2026 session): marks Chris Brown 'Resigned December 13, 2024' and lists Zachary Harvey as the Rutland-3 representative.

transition.note: Francis 'Topper' McFaun resigned the seat in 2026 (the House directory records April 3, 2026). Governor Phil Scott appointed David Soucy to fill the vacancy, effective immediately on April 9, 2026.

sources.note: Office of Governor Phil Scott, press release (April 9, 2026), 'Governor Phil Scott Appoints David Soucy to House of Representatives': the Governor appointed David Soucy of Barre Town to fill the vacant Washington-Orange seat, effective immediately; the release thanks the departing member as 'Topper McFaun'.
Vermont General Assembly, All Representatives directory (2025-2026 session): marks Francis McFaun 'Resigned April 3, 2026' and lists David Soucy as a Washington-Orange representative.

transition.note: Heather Surprenant resigned the seat in September 2025 (the House directory records September 29, 2025). Governor Phil Scott appointed Michael Hoyt to fill the vacancy, effective December 2, 2025.

sources.note: Office of Governor Phil Scott, press release (December 2, 2025), 'Governor Phil Scott Appoints Michael Hoyt to House of Representatives': the Governor appointed Michael Hoyt of West Hartford to fill the vacant Windsor-4 seat, replacing Heather Surprenant, who resigned in September 2025; the appointment is effective December 2, 2025.
Vermont General Assembly, All Representatives directory (2025-2026 session): marks Heather Surprenant 'Resigned Sept. 29, 2025' and lists Michael Hoyt as the Windsor-4 representative.
